newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA expels brokerage and fines partners.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA expels brokerage and fines partners.

text.p: A Birmingham, England-based brokerage and three of its partners have been disciplined for concealing the true state of the firm's finances, the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Thursday.
Griffiths & Lamb, which ceased trading in October 1993, was formally expelled by the SFA and three of its partners were fined over a share placing earlier that year.
The SFA said the firm had placed shares in a Canadian company in a client account, despite the fact that the purchase was contingent on other shares being sold.
To cover the error, the shares to be sold were assigned to other client accounts, before being returned to the original client account two weeks later.
The SFA said Griffiths & Lamb had provided it with false, misleading or inaccurate information in relation to its financial resources between November 1992 and September 1993.
It said the firm had broken five of its principles, including the requirement for high standards of integrity.

Griffiths & Lamb was fined 22,500 stg, equity partner Ivan Griffiths was fined 5,000 stg, equity partner John Hallworth was fined 10,000 stg and Richard Parfitt, a salaried partner and compliance officer, was fined 1,500 stg.
All three individuals were removed from the register of partners and ordered to pay costs.

The SFA said it had taken into account that all amounts due to private clients were settled during its wind-down, and that Parfitt said he had insufficient authority within the firm to carry out his duties effectively.
